items.title: Rossano Sportiello interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, October 2, 2015 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Jack Teagarden, the greatest trombone innovator ever.

ctx.x: I love what you have to say about the music and how important it is to you to get that across to people. Don’t you feel that people listen more intently if things are not so loud?

Oh yeah, of course. Of course. Because it’s the same thing like when you have a very bright light right in your eyes, then you don’t see anything. You are blind completely. And the ears work the same way you know. By the way, something else I wanted to say about the prejudice that sometimes some audiences have against bebop. If you think of Charlie Parker with strings. That’s the most beautiful music that you can imagine, and that’s bebop. He was the king of bebop, Charlie Parker. So and vice versa there is this…
